findings.description: Under the sub-criterion 'Quality and appropriateness of the researcher's professional experience, competences and skills' (1.4), the researcher's demonstrated Earth-observation and machine-learning track record is thin: only three of nine publications touch remote sensing, all recent and all middle-authored, so the current EO/data-science competence is evidenced mainly by mobility and a self-built prototype rather than by a peer-reviewed record. The fellowship is designed to close exactly this gap, but the criterion assesses present competences, so the limited independent EO/ML output is a genuine shortcoming an evaluator would weigh.
findings.evidence: "Of nine publications, only three touch remote sensing, all from 2025 or later and all with her as a middle author; the Earth-observation half of her profile is therefore evidenced not primarily by publications but by hands-on and mobility experience".
findings.recommendation: Strengthen the evidence of applied EO/data-science competence already held — e.g. foreground concrete outputs of the DrR prototype (datasets integrated, models built, validation performed) and any conference/technical outputs — so the current-competence claim rests on more than mobility, without overstating the record.

findings.description: Under 'Soundness of the proposed methodology (... consideration of the gender dimension and other diversity aspects ...)' (1.2), the biological sex/gender dimension is justified as not relevant, which is defensible, but the research does engage people (AgroVIR staff and commercial growers) whose feedback drives the operational-transfer and decision-value evidence, and the sampling of that end-user population is not examined for gender or wider diversity balance. An evaluator may see the diversity treatment of the human-participant strand as incomplete.
findings.evidence: "A biological sex/gender dimension in the research content is therefore not relevant to FIELDWISE ... Where the research does engage people, it does so inclusively and with safeguards: the operational assessment gathers structured feedback from AgroVIR staff and participating commercial growers".
findings.recommendation: Add a brief statement on how diversity is considered in the end-user engagement (e.g. inclusive recruitment of growers/staff for feedback and demonstrations), so the diversity dimension is addressed for the part of the research that does involve people, complementing the reasoned justification for the biological gender dimension.

findings.description: Under 'Quality of the supervision, training and of the two-way transfer of knowledge' (1.3), the quality of supervision during the six-month evaluated placement rests on unconfirmed working assumptions — the on-site supervisor's identity and research grade are declared as operator-provided assumptions to be confirmed later. Because the placement is an integral, evaluated element, the unconfirmed supervision arrangement introduces uncertainty into the otherwise strong supervision case.
findings.evidence: "the placement is planned to be supervised on site by a named senior member of staff at senior research grade ... these placement-host arrangements are operator-provided working assumptions to be confirmed with the company before the placement begins".
findings.recommendation: Confirm and firm up the placement supervision arrangement (named on-site supervisor and grade, and supervisory cadence during M25-M30) so that placement supervision quality is presented as established rather than assumed, matching the specificity of the host-side supervision cadence.

findings.description: Under 'The magnitude and importance of the project's contribution to the expected scientific, societal and economic impacts' (2.3), the magnitude of the societal, environmental and economic impact is asserted almost entirely through output-level KPIs, with the project deliberately declining to quantify any water-saving, economic-benefit or adoption-scale estimate. The refusal to over-claim is credible, but it leaves the outcome-level magnitude largely unsized, which weakens the demonstration of 'magnitude and importance' the criterion asks for.
findings.evidence: "the project does not claim in advance that it will achieve a particular percentage reduction in water use; the environmental benefit will be quantified from project evidence rather than pre-declared."
findings.recommendation: Without pre-committing to unfounded numbers, add credible bounded indicators of potential magnitude (e.g. an illustrative range for irrigation-timing water savings drawn from published literature, or the scale of hectares/growers reachable via the exploitation footprint) framed as context rather than promises, so the magnitude of the societal/economic contribution is sized as well as the outputs.

findings.description: Under 'Suitability and quality of the measures to maximise expected outcomes and impacts ... including communication activities' (2.2), the communication strand is the least developed of the three: it comprises one field demonstration and one public-facing article per year, with the section itself noting these activities carry no deliverable and no KPI, unlike the KPI-anchored dissemination and exploitation measures. The communication plan therefore lacks the measurable targets and audience specificity that would evidence its suitability and quality.
findings.evidence: "one public field demonstration with AgroVIR farmers and one public-facing article per year ... being operator-decided activities, carry no deliverable identifier of their own".
findings.recommendation: Give the communication measures concrete, checkable targets (audiences, channels, indicative reach, timing) and, where possible, tie them to a monitored indicator, so communication is maximised and verifiable on the same footing as the dissemination and exploitation strands.

findings.criterion: Quality and efficiency of the implementation
findings.description: Under 'Quality and capacity of the host institutions and participating organisations, including hosting arrangements' (3.2), several hosting arrangements for the evaluated M25-M30 placement — on-site supervisor and grade, workspace, FMIS and customer-data access, the team joined, and the partner contact's role — rest on descriptions not yet confirmed by AgroVIR. Since the placement is an evaluated part of the action and no letter of commitment is provided, the reliance on unconfirmed hosting arrangements is a genuine shortcoming in the demonstrated capacity of the participating organisation.
findings.evidence: "Several placement-host descriptors (the on-site supervisor and his grade, the workspace and system access, the identity of the team the fellow joins, and the AgroVIR contact's role) rest on descriptions supplied for, but not yet formally confirmed by, the participating organisations".
findings.recommendation: Confirm the placement hosting arrangements with AgroVIR before submission and present them as established facts (supervisor and grade, workspace, system access, hosting team), converting the currently assumed hosting descriptors into confirmed capacity statements to remove the uncertainty around the evaluated placement.

findings.criterion: Quality and efficiency of the implementation
findings.description: Under 'Quality and capacity of the host institutions ... including hosting arrangements' (3.2), the beneficiary has no prior experience of hosting a funded MSCA fellow; the host's readiness is argued from an above-threshold resubmission of the same pairing rather than from a delivered MSCA hosting track record. This is handled honestly, but the absence of prior funded-hosting experience is a legitimate capacity consideration an evaluator would weigh.
findings.evidence: "ELTE has not previously hosted a funded MSCA fellow." ... "This is stated as an application record and an established supervisory relationship, not as prior funded-hosting experience the institution does not have."
findings.recommendation: Reinforce host capacity with concrete evidence of MSCA-relevant support capability (e.g. institutional grants/research-support office services, prior hosting of other international fellowships, HR and researcher-development infrastructure), so the lack of a funded-MSCA hosting record is offset by demonstrable institutional readiness.

findings.criterion: Quality and efficiency of the implementation
findings.description: Under 'appropriateness of the effort assigned to work packages' (3.1), the partner in-kind effort figures that substantiate the implementation and supervision narrative (MATE 2.4 PM, MVCRI 1.5 PM, AgroVIR 3.0 PM, supervisor 2.5 PM, co-supervisor 2.0 PM) are all declared operator estimates to be confirmed, so the appropriateness of the partner contribution rests on unconfirmed values. The fellow's own 30.0 PM allocation is firm, but the partner-effort basis is indicative only.
findings.evidence: "These five figures are operator estimates to be confirmed with the partners; they are presented as indicative rather than committed".
findings.recommendation: Confirm the indicative partner in-kind person-month figures with each participating organisation and present them as committed contributions, so the appropriateness-of-effort argument (particularly the supervisory and placement-host effort) is grounded in confirmed rather than assumed values.

revision_actions.action_description: In Impact 2.3, add bounded, literature-referenced indicators of potential societal/economic/environmental magnitude (e.g. an illustrative irrigation-timing water-saving range and the hectare/grower scale reachable via the exploitation footprint), framed as context rather than commitments, so outcome-level magnitude is sized alongside the output KPIs.

Confirm the AgroVIR placement hosting arrangements (on-site supervisor and grade, workspace, FMIS/customer-data access, hosting team, partner contact role) before submission and restate them in Implementation 3.2 as established capacity rather than working assumptions.

In Excellence 1.4, foreground concrete applied-EO/data-science outputs already achieved (DrR prototype datasets, models and validation, and any technical/conference outputs) to strengthen the current-competence evidence beyond mobility, without overstating the publication record.

In Excellence 1.2, add a short statement on how diversity is considered in the end-user engagement strand (inclusive recruitment of growers and AgroVIR staff for feedback and demonstrations), complementing the reasoned justification that the biological gender dimension is not applicable.

In Excellence 1.3, confirm and specify the placement supervision arrangement (named on-site supervisor, grade and supervisory cadence during M25-M30) so placement supervision quality is presented as established rather than assumed.

In Impact 2.2, give the communication measures concrete targets (audiences, channels, indicative reach and timing) and, where feasible, a monitored indicator, so communication is verifiable on the same footing as the KPI-anchored dissemination and exploitation strands.

In Implementation 3.2, reinforce host capacity with evidence of MSCA-relevant support infrastructure (research-support office services, prior international-fellowship hosting, researcher-development and HR provisions) to offset the absence of a funded-MSCA hosting record.

In Implementation 3.1, confirm the indicative partner in-kind person-month figures with each participating organisation and present them as committed contributions to ground the appropriateness-of-effort argument in confirmed values.
